receipt.initializer: fileprivate in existing BookSourceStore owner file
receipt.revisionScope: Local store revision only; never compare across owners/relaunches. Normal load binds the initial application revision, not later unsaved memory.
receipt.sourceCountMeaning: Published deduped source count on normal reads; actual written snapshot count on saves.

ioContract: MainActor awaits the original normal loader, then borrows the immutable COW library and revision in O(1). No encoding, hashing, source-ID scan, or file IO is added at checkpoint admission.

All saves reuse the existing static persistQueue and concrete streamed writer. SHA256 updates exactly the existing successful 1 MiB chunk writes; returned evidence is exposed as a receipt only after actual FileHandle.close and atomic rename both succeed.
PendingSourceWrite batches are sealed at strict admission; earlier queue closures retain their own batch, and later UI writes cannot be consumed before an older checkpoint and then overwritten by it.

Before-admission cancellation throws; after-admission cancellation does not retract the committed write job or its actual completion receipt. DEBUG exposes one queue observation only, never an arbitrary writer callback or receipt factory.

The existing normal loader opens one final-component no-follow regular-file FD, reads once, closes it, decodes/dedupes, and hashes those original bytes on its existing loadQueue. Only actual POSIX ENOENT produces normalMissingFile; no decode/access/directory/ENOTDIR error becomes missing.

Optional bootstrap calls the same private concrete writer. A successful startup write is explicitly normalBootstrapWrite. Any bootstrap error blocks checked normal-load/save proofs, including an ambiguous rename-before-marker failure.

Legacy UI save, static writeLibrary Void API, reload, logging, flush and queue-barrier APIs are retained and share the real IO primitives. No save-after-readback, alternate cold reload, repair, or new source queue/cache/database is added.

limitations: Swift grammar checks are not SDK compilation, XCTest/Testing execution, or real device validation; 6 methods are definitions only.
Only book_sources.json is covered. Pins sidecar, Cookie/Login/runtime state, book metadata/reading positions, UserDefaults/Keychain and full user-data preservation remain outside this receipt.
Atomic write/close/rename completion is not fsync durability, directory fsync, immunity from later admitted writes, or a multi-file transaction/frozen library.
Initial normal-load proof is immutable historical IO evidence, not proof that current memory or a later disk generation is unchanged. No cross-process or cross-owner generation lock is added.

Legacy constructor pin IO, synchronous ensureLoaded/reloadFromDisk, and existing index/prune work on main remain existing boundaries; new handoff APIs do not use a second reload or add whole-file hashing to the explicit synchronous reload.
The normal loader retains its existing whole-JSON allocation/decoder behavior and practical source capacity; this step does not introduce a new giant-library limit or claim streaming decode.
S5 coordinator/data-handoff caller is not connected in this ignored step; integration and SDK selection must occur after the current 180-source checkpoint.
